OpenKingdoms VERSION_HERE, an engine for Total Annihilation: Kingdoms.

Play in a browser at [openkingdoms.net](https://openkingdoms.net), or download below and play on the desktop.

This release answers a round of playtesting on openkingdoms.net. Your army
looks after itself again. Units stop chasing an enemy to their death,
patrols and guards fight and mend, and blades leave flyers alone. Ships
float, the game options you pick are kept for the next battle, Use
Crusades Units among them, and Ctrl+D works. Everyone in a multiplayer
room has to be on this version, so refresh the page after the update.

## Your army

A unit that picks its own fight gives up once it is its leash from where
the fight began, 500 pixels for most units, and walks back. Until now it
followed a fleeing enemy across the map. Units on Defensive still hold
their ground. (#425)

Patrols fight in any stance but Passive. A patrolling unit breaks off
from its route to fight, comes back to where it left and carries on.
Builders on patrol repair damaged allies they see along the route and
help finish your frames. (#425)

A guard attacks whoever hits the unit it guards, repairs it, and helps it
build or repair whatever it is working on, then goes back to guarding. It
keeps the original's distance from a building it guards instead of
standing inside it. (#426)

Swordsmen and the other melee units no longer strike a flyer in the air.
Archers and other ranged units still can, as in the original. (#425)

## Combat

A splash shot that strikes its target bursts on the target's body and
does its whole damage. Shots used to burst a little short, so a Rictus did
about 560 to a swordsman where the original does 817. (#424)

Ctrl+D self destructs the units you have selected, lodestones included,
after the original's two second countdown, and Ctrl+D again calls it off.
(#426)

The message list names a player who falls, with one of the original's
lines. (#426)

## Game options

The skirmish screen and a game you host remember their options for the
next battle, as the original does: Use Crusades Units, Line of Sight, Map
Revealed, Monarch Expendable, random start positions, cheats, the unit
limit, and on the skirmish screen your side and the enemy's. If your
battles felt harder hitting lately, Use Crusades Units had been switching
itself off. Tick it once and it stays. Players who join a room always play
the host's rules. (#424)

## Ships and spells

Ships ride at their waterline in both views instead of sitting on the sea
floor, and units that wade stand in the water the same way. Thirsha's
lightning leaves her, not the ground under her. (#423)

In the 3D view the ground past the edge of the map is black, as in the
classic view, instead of sky, and a selection ring beside a cliff no longer
climbs it. (#427)

## Multiplayer

A player who leaves a versus game loses their army, as in the original,
and the players left go on at once instead of waiting. The win goes to
whoever stays. (#419, #420)

In a match the in-game menu is the multiplayer one, with no Restart, Save
or Load, and the game keeps running while it is open. (#421)

## Also

In the browser, a Shift whose release the page missed no longer stays
held, so a click on a build button queues one unit again, and Shift+click
five. (#422)

The site counts its visits and battles for a private stats page, without
cookies or anything that tells you apart. The privacy page says what it
keeps. (#415, #417)

## Multiplayer compatibility

Everyone in a room must be on the same version. A room hosted on an older
or newer version is greyed in the list with the reason. After an update,
refresh the page before you host or join, and have everyone else in the
room do the same. Desktop builds older than this one cannot join games
hosted with it, and the other way round. Replays play only on the version
that recorded them.
